title: Surjective affine diagonal ideal class map with actual kernel-unit coordinates
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $U\subset X$ and $V\subset S$ be affine opens with $U\subset f^{-1}V$. Put $A=\Gamma(X,U)$, $R=\Gamma(S,V)$ with the algebra structure induced by $f$, $B=A\otimes_R A$, and $J=\ker(\mu:B\to A)$, where $\mu(a\otimes b)=ab$. Let $p_1,p_2:X\times_S X\to X$ and $\Delta:X\to X\times_S X$ be the projections and diagonal of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], put $W=p_1^{-1}U\cap p_2^{-1}U$, and let $\mathcal I$ be the actual module-sheaf kernel of $\mathcal O_{X\times_S X}\to\Delta_*\mathcal O_X$. Let $C=\Delta^*\mathcal I$ be the tensor-formula diagonal conormal [def-sc-diagonal-conormal], and $\eta$ the canonical tensor-pullback adjunction unit [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. There exist a ring isomorphism $r:B\simeq\Gamma(X\times_S X,W)$ and a surjective $A$-linear map $q:J\to\Gamma(U,C)$, with the $A$-action on $J$ through the first tensor factor, such that $r(1\otimes a)=p_2^*(a)$ and $r(a\otimes1)=p_1^*(a)$ for every $a\in A$. For every inclusion $h:U\subset\Delta^{-1}W$ and every $j\in J$ there exists $s\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal I)$ whose kernel inclusion is $r(j)$ and such that $q(j)$ equals the restriction to $U$ along $h$ of $\eta_W(s)$. No derivation is part of this statement.

proof.text: Put A = Γ(X,U), R = Γ(S,V), B = A ⊗_R A and J = ker(μ:B → A). Since U maps into V, the open W = p₁⁻¹U ∩ p₂⁻¹U is U ×_V U. The affine fibre-product calculation identifies its section ring with B. The ring isomorphism r sends a ⊗ 1 to the first projection pullback and 1 ⊗ a to the second projection pullback. The diagonal inverse image of W equals U, and its restriction to W is the closed immersion induced by μ.

proof.text: Restrict the actual module-sheaf kernel of O → Δ_* O to W. Restriction to an open is exact, and the restricted pushforward is pushforward by the restricted diagonal, so this kernel is the ideal module associated to J. On the affine open W its kernel inclusion is injective with range ker μ. Therefore, for every j in J, there is a unique actual kernel section s whose inclusion equals r(j). This identifies the kernel section module with J, without assuming global quasi-coherence of the diagonal kernel.

proof.text: Restrict the tensor-formula pullback to U. Inverse image and change of rings commute with restriction, so it is tensor pullback of the ideal module by the restricted closed diagonal. Under this identification the adjunction unit is preserved: its inverse-image unit and pure tensor 1 ⊗ s restrict to the corresponding units on the chart. Apply affine_conormal_sections_existence to that restricted closed immersion, not directly to the original diagonal. This identifies actual conormal sections on U with J/J² and sends the restricted adjunction-unit class of the section representing j to the quotient class of j.

proof.text: Compose the quotient class map J → J/J² with the section identification to obtain q. Quotient classes exhaust J/J², so q is surjective. The A-action through the first tensor factor agrees modulo J with multiplication on A and hence with the A-action on actual conormal sections; thus q is A-linear. For every j the kernel section from step 2 and the unit calculation from step 3 give precisely the displayed formula, for any proof of U ≤ Δ⁻¹W. The proof argument of this inclusion is immaterial by proof irrelevance. Empty U gives zero rings and modules, so it introduces no exception.
